relation_to_executors_rounds: none of these 14 mutants appears in mutation_selfcheck_round1/2/4/5/7 or in mutation_selfcheck_verifier_round1; they attack the protocol client's local precondition mirrors, the table-closure mechanism, the run delegation, doctor's stdout purity and the two disclosed limits

classification_glossary.caught-by-card-id: a row named for the property under attack went red
classification_glossary.caught-by-gate-id-only: only rows unrelated to the attacked property went red
classification_glossary.survived: the whole check stayed PASS 89 with the mutant applied
classification_glossary.crashed-mutant-ill-formed: the edit did not compile, so no property was measured
classification_glossary.anchor-missing: the anchor text was not found exactly once

matrix.attack_claim: status really sends session.get when a session is known
the five protocol statuses are each mapped to a graded exit code
the host.configure envelope the CLI sends satisfies the protocol's epoch rule
the command table's method column is checked against what the CLI actually sent
a row's proven_by must name probes that actually drive that row
a row that names no probe cannot support the deliverable
deleting a probe a table row relies on goes red
the command surface never shells out to another program
the published digest proves the installed file was the one launched
matrix.classification_note: the batch-1 run of this mutant failed 19 probe-host rows whose details are all transport errors; three further runs turned rows unrelated to the digest red (INIT once, GO+TABLE-ROWS once) and gave a clean PASS 89 on the third, so the mutant is classified from a run where the fixture host was reachable

matrix.attack_claim: non-interactive stdout is JSONL only for every command (card negative: mixed logs on stdout must fail)
the contract's run syntax reaches the protocol client rather than only the accepted cascade
the client refuses locally what the core would refuse (command_id shape)
the client mirrors the schema's EmptyPayload rule for host.status and session.get
matrix.classification_note: the edit left the strings import unused, so apps/cli did not compile and the gate caught a build break, not the EmptyPayload mirror; re-run well-formed as R2-M13b, which survived

matrix.attack_claim: the client mirrors the published schema's EmptyPayload rule for host.status and session.get, so a stray payload key is refused locally

environment_flake.what: runs of go run ./tests/runtime/cli_contract in which the child CLI could not dial the check process's own in-process 127.0.0.1 listener
environment_flake.measured: of 24 executions by this review, 18 emitted the identical 89 green ids and 6 failed with red rows only in the probe-host phase; the red sets were not stable across attempts (20, 16, 22, 19, 1 and 2 rows) and every failure detail is a transport error (dial tcp 127.0.0.1:<port> connectex timeout, or context deadline exceeded)
environment_flake.consequence: the check grades a lost connection to its own fixture as a product failure instead of not_verified, so the card can read FAIL and PASS minutes later with no source change

survivor_reasons.R2-M1-session-get-leg-always-skipped: no probe ever gives status a session: v2verbs.go writes its config without session_id and never passes --session to status, and the row asserts session.get == SKIPPED, so the first of the contract's two operations for status is neither sent nor tested
survivor_reasons.R2-M2-in-progress-becomes-a-failure: the fixture answers COMPLETED, REJECTED, NOT_IMPLEMENTED, a truncated body and an HTTP 500; it never answers IN_PROGRESS or ACKNOWLEDGED, so two of the five protocol statuses are mapped with no assertion
survivor_reasons.R2-M3-host-configure-carries-the-epoch: this is the one-line fix for the model-switch defect and the check cannot see it: the fixture answers any POST /v2/command with COMPLETED without decoding the envelope, so a switch the real core refuses still exits 0 and still prints status COMPLETED
survivor_reasons.R2-M4-table-claims-a-method-the-code-nev: the method column of the command table is copied into commands/help, but no row compares it with the envelopes the probe recorded; proven_by gates which probes ran, not what the verbs sent
survivor_reasons.R2-M5-proven-by-pointed-at-an-unrelated-: tableRowsProven only asks whether the named id appears in the emitted id list, so naming two rows that run for unrelated reasons (CLI-BUILDS, HEAD-RECORDED) satisfies it
survivor_reasons.R2-M8-os-exec-hidden-in-a-sibling-delive: W0503-NO-PROCESS-DELEGATION reads apps/cli/cli_contract.go by name; cli_v2.go, cli_verbs.go, cli_run_contract.go and cli_run_windows.go are not scanned, so the card's named negative about a shell alias is guarded for one file of the six it delivered
survivor_reasons.R2-M9-candidate-launches-the-build-tree-: the digest row compares bytes and two builds of one source emit byte-identical version records; DIST-INSTALLED-BINARY-DIGEST-RECORDED publishes the installed file's digest but no row compares it, exactly as remediation_round1 disclosed
survivor_reasons.R2-M12-command-id-pattern-mirror-removed: the CLI always mints cmd-<verb>-<pid>, which matches the pattern, so the mirror of the published identifier rule is never exercised from either side
survivor_reasons.R2-M13b-empty-payload-mirror-removed: the CLI sends {} for EmptyPayload methods and no probe asks it to send a stray key, so the local mirror of the schema rule is unexercised

scope.restoration: every mutant restored with git checkout -- <exact path>; restored_clean and restored_sha_matches_baseline are true for all 14; git status --porcelain for apps/cli, tests/runtime and ops is empty at the end
